AI.result: Ancilla-free braiding is achieved via graph deformation. A no-go theorem shows purely unitary input-agnostic fusion is impossible without ancillas, but a qudit reset enables such fusion. Thus ancilla resources are not required for braiding or fusing non-Abelian anyons.
AI.conclusion: The fusion protocol highlights reset as an underutilized primitive for error correction without the spacetime overhead of ancillas and measurements, with implications for experimental error-correction efforts.

title: Boundary-accessible work in a collision-charged topological quantum battery
comment: 26 pages, 20 figures, including Supplemental Material (16 pages, 14 figures)
summary: Quantum batteries store energy in nonequilibrium quantum states. The ergotropy sets the work extractable by an arbitrary global unitary, but a device usually exchanges energy through a single local port. It remains unclear how much stored work such a port can deliver, and whether topological edge modes help. We study a dimerized spin chain of Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) type. Excited two-level ancillas charge it at one end by repeated collisions, and an initially empty two-level load discharges it at the same site. An exact free-fermion mapping yields a bound on the load work for all number-conserving quadratic extraction protocols. The load gains extractable work only if a single-particle mode of the battery holds more than half an excitation. Resonant charging fills the topological edge mode above this threshold. A single boundary pulse then delivers 98.6% of the maximal load work allowed by the bound for representative parameters. Under the same six-collision controls, the trivial-phase load remains passive. Within the protocol that selects the load pulse for maximum delivered work, cycle power peaks at a finite collision number while delivered work continues to increase over the scanned range. Over the tested range, the advantage survives hopping disorder, which preserves chiral symmetry. On-site disorder breaks this symmetry and leaves a finite fraction of loads passive. Topology thus supplies a localized access channel, while spectral matching and symmetry decide whether stored energy becomes usable local work.

AI.tldr: This work establishes how much work a single local port can extract from a quantum battery, using an SSH dimerized spin chain, and shows that resonant charging of a topological edge mode enables near-maximal local work delivery.
AI.motivation: Energy is stored in nonequilibrium quantum states, and ergotropy sets the extractable work under an arbitrary global unitary. However, real devices exchange energy through a single local port, so it is unclear how much stored work such a port can deliver and whether topological edge modes improve delivery. This work addresses the gap between global extractable work and practically accessible local work.
AI.method: The authors study a dimerized spin chain of Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) type. Excited two-level ancillas charge the battery at one end via repeated collisions, and an initially empty two-level load discharges it at the same site. An exact free-fermion mapping is used to derive a bound on the load work valid for all number-conserving quadratic extraction protocols. Charging and discharging are analyzed across topological and trivial phases, with disorder tests for hopping (chiral-symmetry-preserving) and on-site (chiral-symmetry-breaking) cases.
AI.result: The load acquires extractable work only if a single-particle mode of the battery holds more than half an excitation. Resonant charging fills the topological edge mode above this threshold, and a single boundary pulse then delivers 98.6% of the maximal load work permitted by the bound for representative parameters. Under identical six-collision controls, the trivial-phase load remains passive. When the protocol selects the load pulse for maximum delivered work, cycle power peaks at a finite collision number while delivered work keeps increasing over the scanned range. The topological advantage survives hopping disorder that preserves chiral symmetry, whereas on-site disorder breaks chiral symmetry and leaves a finite fraction of loads passive.
AI.conclusion: Topology provides a localized access channel for energy delivery, but spectral matching and symmetry ultimately determine whether stored energy can be converted into usable local work. The results quantify single-port work extraction limits and clarify the combined roles of topology, resonance, and symmetry in quantum battery performance.
